title: There is no cubic 8-circulant nut graph: completing the existence classification of cubic polycirculant nut graphs
exact_endpoint: Nut8.no_cubic_8circulant_nut : Nut8.Target, where Target := ∀ (W : Type) [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] (G : SimpleGraph W) [DecidableRel G.Adj], ¬ (Cubic G ∧ Nut G ∧ Circulant 8 G); Nut: at least two vertices, real adjacency kernel of dimension one containing a full vector; Circulant l: an automorphism whose integer-power orbits number l, all of equal size
scope: Bašić and Damnjanović, On cubic polycirculant nut graphs, arXiv:2411.16904v1 Conjecture 16 = Conjecture 1 of the published version (Comput. Appl. Math. 2025). Their Theorem 2 excludes l in {1,2,4,5} and constructs cubic l-circulant nut graphs for l in {3,6,7} and l >= 9; l = 8 was the only open case. Proof: a single kernel character on semiregular orbit coordinates gives a symmetric signed integral 8x8 quotient with nullity exactly one (injective lift) and nonzero diagonal cofactors; cubicity forces a local grammar; an inductive kernel-checked catalogue of 194 connected subcubic supports with 1,722 isomorphism certificates, 669 augmentations and tree switching reduce to 9,172 signed matrices, each excluded by an exact determinant (8,208) or zero principal cofactor (964) certificate. Valid for all orbit sizes m, without bounding graph order.

substantive_reason: It settles the only open case of a published conjecture (Comput. Appl. Math. 2025) and thereby completes the existence classification of cubic l-circulant nut graphs: they exist exactly for l in {3,6,7} and l >= 9. The proof is a new signed-quotient obstruction valid for every orbit size, beyond the source's unsigned-pregraph method, which left l = 8 unresolved.
